purpose: Defects identified outside the activity that owns them: the seed pass, and anything one activity noticed that another must fix. This file is the Phase 4 denominator — the set every blind sweep is measured against. Entries are resolved here, never moved to the activities ledger.

defects.title: US-11 AC-3 (re-extend when a tool directory returns) has no implementation; the test is a strict xfail
defects.evidence: @pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason="...a recorded tool whose directory returns EMPTY is read as a deletion, so the artifact is removed from every healthy tool before the extension rule is reached (_has_vanished_surface short-circuits). Bytes survive in the archive (NFR-01) but the artifact disappears everywhere..."). Confirmed by running the suite: 745 passed, 1 xfailed.
defects.impact: An acceptance criterion is knowingly unmet, and the failure mode is the worst one the system has: unmounting a tool's directory (a network share, an uninstalled editor) deletes the artifact from every other tool. The xfail is honest, but it means the spec and the code disagree and the resolution needs the spec owner, not a code change.

verification.method: Probe tmp/probe_us11_returning_tool.py, driving the real _settle/sync_once path over the same two-tool workspace the xfail uses, reading the filesystem and the canonical store after each stage.
verification.observed: One artifact (helper.md) settled on claude + cursor. rmtree(cursor) -> cursor unavailable, claude keeps the artifact (correct, FR-04 holds). cursor.mkdir() -> directory returns present but EMPTY. Result: claude EMPTY, cursor EMPTY, canonical store EMPTY. The artifact is destroyed on the tool that never went away AND its canonical record is dropped; only the archive retains bytes (helper.md x2 plus the canonical json). Three further polls heal nothing.
verification.what_was_refuted: The title's framing. This is not 'AC-3 has no implementation' — AC-3 is correctly marked [ ] unchecked in US-11, so an unbuilt AC is not itself a defect. The real finding is a SPEC CONFLICT that the code resolves destructively, and the destruction reaches beyond the returning tool.
verification.mechanism: compute_sync_plan.py:130, `glitched = {tool for tool, count in vanish_count.items() if count >= _GLITCH_THRESHOLD}` with _GLITCH_THRESHOLD = 2 (line 60). A tool that loses two or more recorded artifacts in one poll is treated as glitched and its RemoveArtifact intents are swapped for ReprojectCanonical (US-11 AC-9). The docstring at line 118-119 states the counterpart deliberately: 'A lone vanish is a deliberate deletion and is left to propagate.' So with ONE recorded artifact the guard does not fire, reconcile_known._has_vanished_surface (line 64) short-circuits to removal, and the removal propagates to every tool.
verification.the_asymmetry: A user with two or more synced artifacts is protected by the glitch guard; a user with exactly one loses everything. Exposure is inversely proportional to how much the user syncs, which is the opposite of what anyone would predict.
verification.wider_finding: US-11 AC-3 is phrased entirely as an availability TRANSITION ('Given an agentic_tool's status was unavailable at the previous poll and its directory is present ... at the current poll'). The rebuild does not track per-tool availability across polls at all: sync_once.py:42 count_available_tools computes only a per-poll integer. The transition state was dropped deliberately — the plan records 'Per-tool availability-status transition logging ... Dropped as YAGNI; document the reduced observability. [decision: drop]'. That decision was classified as an observability reduction, but it also orphaned the state US-11 AC-2, AC-3 and AC-5 and NFR-12 are all written in terms of. AC-3 is therefore not merely unbuilt, it is unimplementable as written against the current design. Filed separately as CD-0025.
verification.is_it_live_in_production: The xfail asserts this defect is 'shared with the legacy tree'. The legacy tree carries the same vocabulary (src/agents_sync/{sync,adoption/removal_propagator,adoption/engine,adoption/canonical_projection}.py all reference vanish/glitch), but this was NOT measured against legacy — src/ is reference scope and was not probed. UNRESOLVED and worth resolving, because if the xfail's claim holds this is a live data-loss path in the running daemon today, unlike CD-0012.

defects.title: Scattered function-local imports in the test suite (hidden dependencies)
defects.evidence: grep -rn '^    from |^    import ' tests_new/*.py finds 20+ occurrences across seven files: `from agents_sync.domain_model.sync_plan import AdoptNewArtifact` at 542/572/586/604, `import os` at 514, `import shutil` at 414, plus tests_new/test_agentic_tools_registry.py:155,177, test_parser_bounds.py:100,108, test_canonical_store.py:184,206, test_sync_state_store.py:177. The same modules are imported at the top of the same files for other names — e.g. test_execute_sync_plan.py:23-33 imports eight names from sync_plan but not AdoptNewArtifact, RenameArtifact, or RemoveArtifact.
defects.impact: Hidden dependencies (Fowler): the file header no longer tells you what the module under test needs, and a reader cannot see which intents a test file exercises without reading every body. It is also inconsistent — the same names are imported both ways in one file.

defects.title: A misspelled path key in the user's config TOML is ignored with no error and no warning
defects.evidence: known_keys = {recipe.config_key for d in definitions for recipe in d.surface_recipes} then `for config_key in known_keys: value = overrides.get(config_key)`. The iteration is over the *known* keys, so a key present in the TOML but not in known_keys — `claude_agents_dirs`, `cluade_skills_dir` — is never looked at. The same holds for scalar keys: _validated_poll_interval reads overrides.get("poll_interval_seconds", DEFAULT...), so `pol_interval_seconds = 30` silently yields the 2.0-second default.
defects.impact: The user edits the config, restarts the daemon, and it runs against the default paths as if the file were empty. Nothing in the exit code, the log, or the behaviour distinguishes 'your override applied' from 'your override was a typo'. This module's own docstring says every configuration defect fails closed.

defects.title: An unreadable local canonical is skipped when building the import slug index, so an import mints a duplicate instead of merging
defects.evidence: document = _read_local_document(state_dir, local_id) / `if document is not None: slug_index[...] = local_id`. _read_local_document (line 208) is `except OSError: return None`, and read_canonical_document(raw) also returns None on a corrupt body. The absent entry is indistinguishable from 'no local artifact has this slug', so _resolve_local_id returns None, surviving_id stays the imported id, and _decide reports merged=False, displaced=False.
defects.impact: The import writes a second canonical for an artifact the user already has, under a different id and the same slug. The next poll then has two artifacts competing for one filename — exactly the collision the reconciliation key exists to prevent. The preview shown to the user (AC-18) reports no merge and no displacement, so the operator has no signal either.

defects.title: _modified_time returns the epoch on any stat failure, indistinguishable from a real 1970 mtime
defects.evidence: try: return path.stat().st_mtime / except OSError: return 0.0. The docstring justifies it as a stat race, but the handler is not scoped to that: EACCES on a directory the daemon cannot traverse, or ENAMETOOLONG, produce the same 0.0. That value feeds freshest() in winner selection.
defects.impact: A surface the daemon cannot stat for a persistent reason loses every freshest-content tiebreak forever, so the user's edits on that tool are perpetually overwritten by the other tool's copy, with no log line. Narrowing the catch to FileNotFoundError would keep the documented race handling and make the rest loud.

defects.title: Failure to install SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers is reported only at DEBUG
defects.evidence: except (OSError, ValueError): _LOGGER.debug("signal %s not installable; relying on stop_event", sig). Since no logging is configured anywhere in the package (see CD-0021), DEBUG is unreachable; even with configuration it is off by default.
defects.impact: The daemon's documented clean-shutdown path (US-07 AC-2) is gone and nobody is told. An operator sending SIGTERM sees the process ignore it and reaches for SIGKILL, which is the one signal that can interrupt a write transaction.

defects.title: rules_source_body is written into every rules canonical and never read by any production code
defects.evidence: tool_bags.setdefault(resolved.tool, {})["rules_source_body"] = parsed.body. grep -rn rules_source_body src_new tests_new returns exactly four hits: this line, its docstring at line 186, and two assertions in tests_new/test_read_tool_surfaces.py (499, 509). No renderer, no dialect, and no executor path consults the key.
defects.impact: Write-only state that inflates every rules canonical and its digest, and — worse — the docstring's promise ("the user's directive-bearing source body is preserved for the origin tool") is believed by the next engineer while nothing restores it.

defects.title: rename_artifact's pending 4-tuple carries a computed write path that is never read
defects.evidence: pending.append((new_surface, old_file, final_text, None)) (108) and pending.append((new_surface, target_file(new_surface), final_text, stale)) (115); the consumer is `for new_surface, _write_file, final_text, stale_location in pending:` (119). The second element is discarded, and target_file(new_surface) at line 115 exists only to be discarded.
defects.impact: A reader has to work out that the two branches deliberately store different paths there and that neither matters. Deleting the element narrows the tuple to three and removes one call.

defects.title: project_canonical's pending 3-tuple carries the same never-read render path
defects.evidence: pending_writes: list[tuple[ToolSurface, Path, str]], appended at line 83 as (target, render_file, new_text), consumed at line 87 as `for target, _render_file, new_text in pending_writes:`. render_file is already recomputable from target via target_file, and write_surface_content recomputes it anyway.
defects.impact: Same cost as CD-0008, and the repetition of the pattern makes it look intentional. Both are deletable in one pass.

defects.title: The only tests for US-15 source-body preservation assert the bookkeeping bag, never that the origin file keeps its directives
defects.evidence: Both references to the feature are read-phase introspection: assert observation.parsed.per_tool_only["claude"]["rules_source_body"] == "@extra.md" (line 499) and assert "rules_source_body" not in ... (line 509). No test drives read -> plan -> execute and then re-reads the origin tool's rules file to check the @import line survived a write.
defects.impact: The suite is green on a promise the system does not keep (see CD-0011). A test that stops at the intermediate value cannot catch the missing second half of the feature.

defects.title: Reprojecting a rules artifact overwrites the origin tool's @import directives with their inlined expansion
defects.evidence: The read phase replaces the body with the inlined text (read_tool_surfaces.py:204: parsed=replace(parsed, body=effective_body, ...)) and stashes the original under rules_source_body. project_canonical then renders every recorded target from that canonical — new_text = canonical_to_file(canonical, target, prior_text) — with no branch consulting rules_source_body and no per-tool special case. The origin tool is one of targets (it is a recorded surface), so the first reprojection after any cross-tool edit rewrites the user's AGENTS.md with the imported files' contents spliced in place of the @extra.md line.
defects.impact: The user's chosen composition — one short rules file pointing at shared fragments — is silently flattened, and the pointer is gone, so subsequent edits to the imported file no longer take effect. Bytes survive in the archive (NFR-01), but the user must notice and restore them.

verification.development_status_evidence: An explicitly scheduled, UNTICKED plan step. docs/architecture_implementation_plan.md:350 — "| S23g | Rules-surface projection render restore | ... |" — carries no checkmark, unlike its neighbour "S23i ✓ (0.7.58)". Plan lines 165-168 list it under "Pre-cutover completion" with [decision: fix before cutover]. The register files it as "F2 — Rules-surface projection render leak. HIGH / latent correctness bug". The read half of US-15 was built in src_new; the write half was never ported. The legacy tree DOES implement the restore (src/agents_sync/rules_io.py:260-262), so this is an unported regression against a story marked Implemented, not a mis-implementation.
verification.method: Three probes under tmp/ driving the real entry point sync_once over tmp_path tool roots with the real claude + codex registry definitions. Independently re-run by the orchestrator: tmp/probe_rules_import_reprojection.py.
verification.observed:
Authored ~/.claude/AGENTS.md of "# My rules
@extra.md
tail line
" becomes, after POLL 1: front matter carrying pair_id, name, and a literal rules_source_body: "# My rules
@extra.md
tail line" key, over a body of "# My rules
SHARED FRAGMENT LINE

tail line". The live @extra.md directive is gone from the body; the original body is emitted into the user's own front matter as a machine key. Stable thereafter — polls 5 and 6 report changed=0, no churn, no escaping blow-up. The imported extra.md is untouched on disk, and the pre-adoption file is archived byte-for-byte (NFR-01 holds).
verification.what_was_refuted: Both the trigger and the severity framing. (1) Reprojection is NOT the trigger and content_intents.py:76 is not the first offender: the defect fires on the FIRST poll via the adoption write at identity_intents.py:66, needing no cross-tool edit — only an @import-bearing rules file present when the daemon starts. So it is MORE reachable than claimed. (2) The finding says bytes survive only in the archive; in fact the original body is written verbatim into the same file as the leaked front-matter key and is also in the canonical, so recovery is in-place. Loss is of the live pointer, not of the bytes.
verification.what_was_upheld: grep -rn rules_source_body src_new/ returns exactly one hit — the write at read_tool_surfaces.py:200. Zero consumers. The origin tool is a projection target like any other; no "don't write back to where it came from" rule exists.
verification.root_cause_correction: The defect is in the SHARED render path — translation.canonical_to_file -> dialects/field_mapping.project_canonical_to_fields:96-97, `for key, value in values["per_tool_only"].get(tool, {}).items(): fields[key] = value` — which copies rules_source_body out as a literal front-matter field instead of consuming it as a render instruction. That path has FOUR call sites: content_intents.py:76 and identity_intents.py:66, :105, :110. None consults rules_source_body.
verification.severity_revision: Lowered as loss, raised as reach. HIGH within the pre-cutover set (matching the register's own F2 rating), MEDIUM in absolute terms: no bytes are unrecoverable. The flag data-loss-risk is retained because the user's live directive is destroyed on disk without consent, but the entry no longer claims unrecoverable loss.

defects.resolution: Deferred to plan step S23g, which already owns it and is marked fix-before-cutover. Not fixed under the cleaning ladder, because the ladder does not own scheduled build work. Unblocked when S23g lands. Two products of this verification were applied rather than deferred: the S23g plan row's scope was corrected to name the shared render path and all four call sites (it previously named only field_mapping + content_intents, leaving the adopt path that actually fires first out of scope), and the US-15 semantics question the probes exposed is filed as CD-0024.

defects.title: Renaming a skill deletes it from every tool and creates nothing in its place
defects.evidence: MEASURED at the real entry point, not inferred. _renamed_surface (line 201) computes the new location as location.with_name(f"{slugify_name(new_name)}{location.suffix}"). Its own docstring covers only two cases — "a new filename stem for a per-file surface, a new slot key for a keyed-map slot" — and a skill is a third that was never added. A skill's location is <slug>/SKILL.md, so with_name yields <old_slug>/renamed.md instead of <new_slug>/SKILL.md, and therefore skill_folder(new_surface) == skill_folder(old_surface). Line 120 write_surface_content replace_directory_atomic's the renamed skill INTO the old folder; line 122 _remove_stale_location then shutil.rmtree's that same folder. The rename deletes its own output. The comment at lines 111-113 asserts "the auxiliary files travel to the new slug via the canonical, so the old folder is retired entire" — a new slug folder that _renamed_surface never produces.
defects.impact: One poll after a user edits `name:` in a SKILL.md: SKILL.md and every auxiliary file are gone from every participating tool, the archive holds SKILL.md copies only, SyncState points at a nonexistent <old_slug>/<new-slug>.md, and the poll reports SyncResult(changed=2, failed=(), blocked=()) — success. Three further polls return changed=0; nothing heals. Direct breach of NFR-01 ("shall not cause loss of user-authored content under any operation") and of US-04 AC-2 ("its file or folder is renamed to match the new slug"). Mitigated only by the stored canonical retaining the bytes, making it recoverable by hand from <state_dir>/canonical/<id>.json — nothing on disk restores it.

verification.development_status_evidence: Not a plan item. docs/architecture_implementation_plan.md line 352 marks S23i complete — "S23i ✓ (0.7.58) ... identity_intents (a renamed skill retires its whole old folder)" — landed in commit d7ea8ee. The folder-retirement behaviour is claimed as delivered. docs/audits/cutover_loose_ends_register_2026_07_12.md line 121 closes the rename amendment as "realized-by-rebuild" with the residual action "verify US-04 AC coverage in the behavioural conformance set" still outstanding — believed built, never verified.
verification.method: Three probes under tmp/, each driving the real entry point sync_once(state_dir, resolved, state, {}, tool_definitions=(claude, cursor)) over real skill folders — never the executor directly with a hand-built plan, so the scenario cannot be an unreachable one. Independently re-run by the orchestrator: tmp/probe_skill_rename_full_tree.py.
verification.observed: After one poll renaming name: demo -> name: renamed, with <skills>/demo/{SKILL.md, references/detail.md} on both tools: old path absent, new path never created, both skills directories empty (rglob('*') == []). Archive holds four SKILL.md.<token>.<timestamp> entries and no copy of references/detail.md. Polls 2, 3, 4 all changed=0.
verification.what_was_refuted: The sweeper's causal story. It claimed a STALE stored canonical drops an un-absorbed auxiliary file, making the loss racy and narrow ("the window is small"). False: reconcile_known._absorb_change emits AbsorbToolEdit before RenameArtifact in the same plan, execute_sync_plan walks intents in order, and read_tool_surfaces._attach_auxiliary_files folds the whole on-disk folder into parsed.auxiliary_files in the same poll — so by the time rename_artifact calls load_canonical the canonical is fresh. Measured: after the rename the canonical contained references/notes.md, a file created seconds before the poll and never previously absorbed. The real defect needs no race at all and is unconditional.
verification.what_was_upheld: The flag (data-loss-risk), the file, the symbol rename_artifact, and the approximate line. Also upheld: _archive_surface_bytes passes the SKILL.md path to archive_copy, never skill_folder(surface), so the archive never covers auxiliary files — archive_copy itself would recurse (shutil.copytree) if handed a directory.
verification.severity_revision: Raised. The sweeper called the window small; there is no window. Critical as a defect, but zero production blast radius today because src_new/ is not cut over and the live daemon runs the legacy src/ tree. MUST-FIX-BEFORE-CUTOVER, not an incident.
verification.coverage_hole: grep -rn rename over tests_new/test_skill_surface.py, test_skill_auxiliary_propagation.py and test_sync_once.py returns nothing. 745 green tests and not one renames a skill. Filed separately as CD-0023.

proposed_remedy.note: Recorded for activity 4.a; not applied. Remedy risks are the reason this is written down rather than fixed on sight.
steps: _renamed_surface must branch on surface.kind == SKILL_KIND and return location.parent.parent / slugify_name(new_name) / SKILL_FILENAME rather than location.with_name(...).

_archive_surface_bytes should pass skill_folder(surface) or location to archive_copy, which already handles a directory. This also closes CD-0017 (the skill_folder docstring claiming auxiliary files are archived and removed with the artifact) and the same gap in remove_artifact (CD-0013).
risks: reject_shared_write_file compares target_file(surface), the SKILL.md path. After the fix, two skills renamed to the same slug collide at FOLDER level, so the collision guard and US-04 AC-5's RejectCollision must key on the folder for skill surfaces or the guard silently stops guarding.
Archiving whole folders enlarges archive entries; the NFR-07 tiered GC prunes directory entries via _remove_entry's shutil.rmtree, a path exercised far less than the file path. Needs a test.
RecordedSurface.location for skills must keep pointing at <new_slug>/SKILL.md so the next poll's observation matches, or the rename converges to a phantom removal.
_remove_stale_location should assert stale != skill_folder(new_surface) — a cheap invariant that would have made this defect loud instead of silent, and worth adding regardless.

defects.title: remove_artifact leaves a skill's folder and every auxiliary file on disk
defects.evidence: For a non-keyed-map surface remove_surface_content returns None (translation.py:113), so the loop takes surface_file.unlink(). For a skill, target_file(surface) is <skills>/<slug>/SKILL.md, so only the front page is deleted and <slug>/references/* remains. rename_artifact handles the same case differently one function above: `stale = skill_folder(old_surface) or old_file` then _remove_stale_location does shutil.rmtree. Same module, two answers to the same question.
defects.impact: A removed skill leaves an orphan directory the read phase skips forever (no SKILL.md -> continue in _observe_skill_folder), so it is invisible to the daemon and accumulates. The asymmetry with rename means whichever behaviour is correct, one of the two is a bug.

defects.title: load_runtime_config creates a directory on the filesystem
defects.evidence: parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) runs inside the call chain of a function named load_runtime_config, on every invocation including the CLI's export, import, and prune paths and every test that merely wants a parsed config. The module docstring acknowledges it ("the only side effect is creating the state directory") rather than resolving it.
defects.impact: A load_ that mutates the filesystem surprises callers and makes config validation untestable without a writable home. Pointing --config at a file with a typo'd state_path silently creates a stray directory tree the operator never asked for.

defects.title: SurfaceRecipe is one dataclass whose trailing fields are inert for three of its four layouts
defects.evidence: The docstring states the design outright: "The trailing fields apply to some layouts and not others; each names the layout it belongs to. An unused one is inert, never consulted for a layout that has no use for it." filename_suffix is read only under Layout.DIRECTORY, candidate_filenames and default_artifact_name only under Layout.RULES_FILE. Every consumer branches on the enum: read_tool_surfaces.read_tool_surfaces (line 58) and _projection_location (line 361) each `match resolved.recipe.layout`. This is the catalogue's own detection signature — a conditional keyed on a kind field the caller supplies, with callers using disjoint subsets.
defects.impact: Cheap today (three optional fields), but it is the shape that grows: each new layout adds fields every other layout carries and ignores, and the type system stops being able to say which combinations are legal. Filed as an observation rather than a defect — commit 8ae638d deliberately collapsed four layout classes into this one, and duplication is cheaper than a wrong abstraction, so this may be the intended trade. Worth revisiting only if a fifth layout arrives.

defects.title: test_execute_sync_plan.py is 934 lines against the project's 500-line file limit
defects.evidence: wc -l gives 934, nearly twice the stated limit and more than twice the largest source module (read_tool_surfaces.py, 444). It covers four separable executor families in one file — content (absorb/project/rebuild), identity (adopt/absorb-into-managed/rename/remove), keyed-map slots, and skill folders — mirroring two production modules (content_intents.py, identity_intents.py) that are already split. Three sibling test modules also breach the limit: test_compute_sync_plan.py (619), test_read_tool_surfaces.py (612), test_mcp_server.py (507).
defects.impact: Every executor change edits the same file, so concurrent work collides there. It is also where the local-import habit is worst — nine `from agents_sync... import` statements inside test bodies (lines 261, 381, 541, 542, 572, 586, 604, 631, 659) because the top-of-file import block has grown unwieldy.

defects.title: skill_folder docstring claims auxiliary files are archived and removed with the artifact; neither happens
defects.evidence: Docstring: "the auxiliary files beside it belong to the same artifact and are written, archived and removed with it (S23i)." Archived: _archive_surface_bytes (identity_intents.py:190) calls archive_copy(execution.state_dir, artifact_id, surface.tool, location) where location is the SKILL.md path, not skill_folder(surface) — only SKILL.md is copied. Removed: remove_artifact (identity_intents.py:151) calls surface_file.unlink(), again the SKILL.md path only. Written is the one of the three that is true (write_surface_content uses replace_directory_atomic).
defects.impact: The docstring is the contract the next engineer reads before touching the skill path; two thirds of it is false, and both false parts concern data preservation.

defects.title: parser_bounds.__all__ omits three names other modules import from it
defects.evidence: __all__ lists eight names and omits MAX_SKILL_AUXILIARY_FILES, MAX_SKILL_FOLDER_BYTES, and read_bytes_bounded. All three are imported by skill_auxiliary_files.py:26-31 (from agents_sync.parser_bounds import MAX_SKILL_AUXILIARY_FILES, MAX_SKILL_FOLDER_BYTES, ParserBoundsExceeded, read_bytes_bounded). The skill bounds were added after the list was written and the list was not updated.
defects.impact: __all__ is the module's declared public surface; it now says less than the truth, so a future reader trusting it could treat read_bytes_bounded as private and break skill_auxiliary_files. Nothing star-imports this module, so deleting __all__ entirely is the cheaper fix.

defects.title: Registry docstring still names the SurfaceSpec type that no longer exists
defects.evidence: "``surface_specs_for`` turns one definition plus the runtime-resolved paths into the read phase's ``SurfaceSpec``s." grep -rn SurfaceSpec src_new tests_new finds no such class — the type is ResolvedRecipe (commit ff217c7, "collapse the parallel Spec hierarchy into ResolvedRecipe"). The same stale name survives in tests_new/test_agentic_tools_registry.py:5, and the leftover parameter name surface_specs in read_tool_surfaces.py:48 and :327 now annotates tuple[ResolvedRecipe, ...].
defects.impact: A reader greps for SurfaceSpec to understand the read phase's input and finds nothing. Half-finished renames are how a codebase acquires two vocabularies for one concept.

defects.title: No logging configuration anywhere, so every INFO-level audit record the CLI emits is discarded
defects.evidence: grep -rn "basicConfig|dictConfig|addHandler|setLevel" src_new tests_new returns zero hits. __main__.py is three lines: `from agents_sync.command_line_interface import main` / `raise SystemExit(main())`. With no root handler and no level set, Python's logging defaults to the handler of last resort at WARNING, so every _LOGGER.info(...) is dropped: _gc_once's "archive GC: scanned %d, deleted %d, reclaimed %d bytes" (command_line_interface.py:177), _export's report (line 128), _import's accepted/skipped counts (line 154), and _log_preview's merge/displacement enumeration (line 166). poll_daemon._install_stop_signals's _LOGGER.debug (poll_daemon.py:44) is likewise unreachable.
defects.impact: The operator has no record of what an import merged, what an export shipped, or what the GC deleted — precisely the consequential, irreversible operations. The code reads as if it audits itself and does not. Debugging a wrong merge after the fact is impossible.

defects.title: GC records which archive entries it deleted, then throws the list away
defects.evidence: prune_archive fills GcReport.deleted_paths entry by entry (artifact_archive.py:176: report.deleted_paths.append(entry)), but _gc_once logs only three integers: "archive GC: scanned %d, deleted %d, reclaimed %d bytes". grep -rn deleted_paths src_new shows the field is read nowhere in production — only in tests_new/test_artifact_archive.py:184.
defects.impact: Archive pruning is the one irreversible deletion of user bytes the daemon performs on its own schedule. A count tells nobody which artifact's history was thinned. Either log the paths or delete the field; carrying it and discarding it is the worst of both.

defects.title: TOCTOU between the size check and the read in the bounded readers
defects.evidence: size = path.stat().st_size / if size > limit: raise / return path.read_text(encoding=encoding). The docstring asserts "a multi-GB hostile file never lands in memory", but nothing pins the file between the stat and the read — a file that grows (or a symlink retargeted) after the stat is read in full. read_bytes_bounded (line 113) has the identical shape, and it is the one used for skill auxiliary files, which may be arbitrarily many.
defects.impact: The DoS bound this module exists to enforce (SEC-C-01/02) can be bypassed by a writer racing the daemon's poll. Low severity because the attacker needs write access to the user's own config directories, but the docstring states a guarantee stronger than the code provides. Reading with a bounded read(limit+1) on an open handle would close it.

defects.title: No test in the rebuild suite renames a skill, so US-04 AC-2 is unverified for the skill kind
defects.evidence: grep -rn rename over tests_new/test_skill_surface.py, tests_new/test_skill_auxiliary_propagation.py and tests_new/test_sync_once.py returns nothing. The rebuild suite is 745 passed / 1 xfailed and contains no skill-rename case. US-04 AC-2 requires that on a rename "its file or folder is renamed to match the new slug; each previously-named file or folder is archived before its rename", and US-04's Notes put skills explicitly in scope ("three support skill, but the algorithm does not depend on these counts").
defects.impact: This is the exact verification the cutover register deferred — docs/audits/cutover_loose_ends_register_2026_07_12.md line 121 closes the rename amendment as "realized-by-rebuild" with residual action "verify US-04 AC coverage in the behavioural conformance set". The gap let a total-data-loss defect (CD-0012) sit in a fully green suite: renaming a skill deletes it from every tool, and nothing failed.

defects.title: US-15 does not say whether a rules file's @import structure survives its tool losing the freshness race
defects.evidence: MEASURED. Probe tmp/probe_rules_import_project_site.py settles a plain two-tool rules artifact, then introduces @extra.md into claude while codex is edited more recently. absorb_tool_edit stores the WINNER's parsed canonical wholesale (content_intents.py:45 save_canonical(execution.state_dir, canonical)), and the winner (codex) never saw claude's per_tool_only bag. Observed on claude after the reprojection poll: "live '@extra.md' directive survives in body: False", "front matter leaks rules_source_body: False" — the whole bag is discarded, so the source body is then preserved ONLY in the archive. US-15 AC-2 requires "the source file's import directives are preserved verbatim ... not flattened on the tool that authored it" but is silent on what happens when that tool is outvoted on freshness.
defects.impact: This is a governance question, not a code defect, and it is load-bearing for the S23g fix: a render-layer-only restore cannot recover the source body in this arm, because the bag is gone before any render runs. Deciding S23g's scope requires knowing whether the origin's @import structure is meant to survive being outvoted. Filed to activity 0 because resolving it means changing the spec or the code, and the acceptance criterion is a governance artifact needing the owner's ruling.
